report:
Likely difference: Model B is more “news/media/entertainment coverage” tilted.

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens across many deep layers and early positions repeatedly point to headline/news and pop-culture vocabulary: “headline(s)”, “Driver”, “Names”, “Royals”, “Manny”, “Vincent”, “Hunter”, “podcast”, “UFO”.
- Strong, repeated tragedy/disaster/reporting terms: “tragic”, “tragedy”, “victims”, “refugees”, “hurricane”, “law”, “leaders”, and even “died” is top-ranked at L17 pos2–4.
- Arts/entertainment descriptors common in reviews/features: “iconic”, “vivid”, “colorful”, “timeless”, “lush”, “melodic”, “vibrant”, “rocker”, “furry”.
- Formatting/lead cues consistent with headlines and ledes: “coming/Coming”, “nearing”, “Sept”, “Emer(…)”, plus many proper-noun tokens (“van”, “von”, accented names).
- The signal is concentrated in mid-to-deep layers and the very first tokens (huge norms at pos0 and growing through layers 18–25), which fits a high-level stylistic/domain shift rather than a low-level lexical quirk.

Given this pattern, Model B appears more inclined toward news-style or culture-coverage language than Model A.
